The triage role copies the reviewer's tool grant byte for byte, so `    tools: [read, write, grep, find, ls]` stopped being unique in fleet.example.yaml and collation-contract.battery.ts's RV15/RV16 matched it 2x. A two-match anchor mutates whichever line the replacer reaches first, so those entries would have kept passing while testing something other than their `what:`. Re-anchored through append_system_prompt_file: ./roles/reviewer.md, which is the spelling RV17 already used for the live config. TWO GOTCHAS worth keeping: mutation-anchors.test.ts reads BOTH the battery and its target at git HEAD, so a working-tree fix looks like it changed nothing until committed; and it truncates the anchor to 70 chars in the message, so a re-anchored entry still prints as the bare line it used to be.

git_lesson: An earlier orchestrator commit claimed test/unit/role-briefings.test.ts and did not contain it. `git add` aborts the ENTIRE invocation when any one pathspec does not match, the invocation named a file a later rename had already moved, and its stderr went to /dev/null -- so it staged nothing and said nothing, while the commit still succeeded on what `git mv` had already staged. Every check afterwards read the WORKING TREE, where the fix was present, so a green suite kept confirming a state the branch did not have. Stage one path per add when the list is heterogeneous; never redirect its stderr.
orchestrator_commit_rule: ALWAYS `git commit -- <paths>`. Two agents share one checkout, so the index is shared and the window between an engineer's `git add` and its `git commit` is a race. A bare orchestrator commit took 1,094 of an engineer's staged lines under a documentation-count message. Split apart, index restored, content verified byte-identical by sha256 -- but the fix is the rule, not the recovery.
